result.title: OCELOT: Planetary-Scale Species Distribution Modeling with Satellite Foundation Embeddings
result.summary: Large-scale repositories of species observations now contain billions of occurrence records from around the world, but these sightings cluster heavily in human-accessible areas. Existing models use only a small fraction of these records and are not evaluated on extrapolating to remote, unvisited regions--where species distribution models can be used as geographic priors to help classify data from camera traps and acoustic recorders. We scale relative occurrence species distribution models by training a multimodal implicit neural representation network called OCELOT that fuses spatial coordinates with satellite foundation embeddings on two orders of magnitude more observations than previous work: 2 billion GBIF records across 100,000 taxa. Scaling to this regime requires co-designing the data pipeline, taxonomic representation, loss formulation, and model architecture: spatiotemporal thinning and sub-linear cell sampling correct for spatial redundancy and observer bias, while an additive taxonomic readout shares representations across species, genera, and families to improve predictions for rare taxa. To evaluate performance in remote areas, we benchmark geographic extrapolation using the NDCG metric on spatial block holdouts up to 600 km. Satellite foundation embeddings improve extrapolation by 51% over coordinate-only models and outperform classical bioclimatic rasters. The resulting model also matches or outperforms existing baselines on established interpolation benchmarks, demonstrating that optimizing for geographic extrapolation does not compromise in-distribution accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文面向行星尺度物种分布建模，用隐式神经表示网络将空间坐标与卫星基础模型嵌入融合，在 20 亿条 GBIF 记录上训练，并配合分类阶元加性读出与空间稀疏采样，以 NDCG 在 600 km 空间块留出上评测地理外推。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关系，但用卫星嵌入作为视觉证据先验、以隐式神经场压缩空间信息并显式评测分布外外推，可供核查“视觉证据如何进入内部表示并支持泛化”这一问题。
